paper_title: NanoTherm: An Analytical Fourier-Boltzmann Framework for Full Chip Thermal Simulations

linked_assets.kind: thesis document (detailed Fourier-BTE solution and validation, cited as reference [15]); not a code or data repository

scenario.figure_or_table: Test Case 3, Figure 6a/6b (text on PDF page 6)
scenario.description: Steady-state full-chip Fourier thermal profile of a single Alpha21264 core with 15 functional units plus an L2 cache. The chip is 16 mm x 16 mm x 0.15 mm. Per-unit power densities come from HotSpot and are shown only graphically in Fig. 6a. The paper reports an RMS error of 0.047 C (max error 3.2%) against COMSOL. Block coordinates and power values are not published numerically.
scenario.architecture: Single-core Alpha21264 floorplan with L2 cache, 16 mm x 16 mm x 0.15 mm silicon die; 10 mm x 10 mm x 3.52 mm heat spreader used in the Fourier setup (silicon k = 150 W/mK, spreader+TIM k = 256 W/mK); adiabatic chip edges; top of spreader held at ambient
scenario.workload: Per-functional-unit power densities obtained from HotSpot (Fig. 6a); no workload or benchmark named
scenario.operating_point: Steady state; 0.2 mm grid discretization; power density per unit given only graphically in Fig. 6a

original_setup.solver: NanoTherm analytical Green's function solver for the steady-state Fourier heat equation (Hankel transform, with edge/corner folding correction for adiabatic boundaries), implemented in R 3.5.1. Results are validated against COMSOL 5.3b (PDF pages 3-6).
original_setup.optimizer: None. The paper is a thermal-simulation speed and accuracy study and uses no floorplan or design optimizer.
original_setup.controller: None. There is no thermal controller or DTM policy; the scenario is a static steady-state power map.
original_setup.benchmark: Test Case 3: single-core Alpha21264 floorplan with 15 functional units plus an L2 cache, on a 16 mm x 16 mm x 0.15 mm die. Per-unit power densities come from HotSpot and appear only graphically in Fig. 6a (PDF pages 6-7). The paper reports RMS error 0.047 C and max error 3.2% against COMSOL.

thermal_observable.location: Calculated full-chip temperature-rise map of the silicon die for the Alpha21264 test case (Fig. 6b, PDF page 7). Only a color map is published; no numeric peak or per-block temperature is given.
thermal_observable.aggregation: Spatial 2D field map at steady state on a 0.2 mm grid. No peak, mean or per-block value is reported numerically. The only numeric figures are the error vs COMSOL (RMS 0.047 C, max 3.2%), which are error metrics rather than temperatures.

physical_mismatches.reason: The original model is a two-layer package (silicon die plus a 3.52 mm heat spreader with TIM) with an isothermal ambient-temperature boundary at the top of the spreader and adiabatic chip edges. It has no heat sink fins, convection model, interposer or 3D stack. A Studio run with different package, cooling and boundary conditions will not reproduce it.

The solver differs fundamentally. The paper uses an axisymmetric Hankel-transform Green's function, with square sources mapped to equal-area circular sources and sampled at grid centres, and validates against COMSOL. A numerical grid solver in Studio is a different method and will not give the same temperatures.

The paper text is internally inconsistent about geometry. The Alpha21264 die is 16 mm x 16 mm, while the Fourier setup lists a 10 mm x 10 mm x 3.52 mm heat spreader. The spreader footprint for this test case is unclear.

The power inputs are per-unit power densities shown only graphically in Fig. 6a. No numeric block powers, areas or coordinates are published, so no complete numeric experiment can be reconstructed from the paper alone.

The transient analysis, the BTE/nanometer-scale model and the reliability aspects of the paper are not part of the selected steady-state Fourier test case and are out of scope. No optimizer or controller exists in the original, so none can be matched.

missing_inputs: Numeric x_m, y_m, width_m and height_m for each of the 15 Alpha21264 functional units and the L2 cache. Fig. 6a gives only a graphical layout, and no HotSpot .flp file is pinned in the packet.
Numeric per-block power or power density (W or W/cm2), with names. Values exist only graphically in Fig. 6a, and no digitized values with uncertainty are supplied.
Total chip power for the Alpha21264 case, which is not stated. It must not be inferred or split across blocks without a published rule.
Heat spreader footprint for the 16 mm die, since the paper's 10 mm x 10 mm spreader conflicts with the die size.

Ambient temperature value Ta, convection or heat-sink boundary parameters, and TIM thickness for this case. Only the isothermal top boundary and effective conductivities (silicon 150 W/mK, spreader+TIM 256 W/mK) are described.
Numeric temperature values for Fig. 6b (peak, mean or per-block). Only the colour map and error metrics are published.

Pinned packet assets: the packet lists none (assets: []). The linked thesis (ref [15], http://www.cse.iitd.ac.in/~srsarangi/files/thesis/shashank.pdf, PDF page 8) is not pinned and so cannot serve as evidence. No code, data or configuration repository is linked in the paper.
Bundled Studio package and material assumptions, which are not provided in the packet and so are not recorded here.
No power time series is needed for this steady-state case, but no workload trace is provided either.
